questions.prompt: Which format is usually the smallest for photographs (with a fallback still recommended)?
questions.explanation: AVIF usually gives the smallest files for photos, with WebP and JPEG as fallbacks (served via <picture>). PNG is for graphics/transparency; GIF should be replaced by video.

questions.prompt: Match each image feature to what it does.

pairs.right: Lists image sources with width descriptors
Tells the browser how wide the image will display
Provides format fallback or art direction

questions.explanation: srcset + sizes let the browser pick the right resolution; <picture> handles format/crop fallback; loading=lazy defers off-screen images.

questions.prompt: The HTML element used to offer multiple image formats (with a fallback) or different crops per breakpoint is the ____ element.
questions.explanation: The element wraps several options (by type for format, or media for art direction) plus an fallback.

questions.prompt: Which are good image-optimization practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use AVIF/WebP with a JPEG fallback
Always set width and height (or aspect-ratio)
Add loading="lazy" to the LCP image

questions.explanation: Responsive sizes, modern formats with fallback, and set dimensions all help. Lazy-loading the LCP image is the one thing to avoid — it delays LCP.

questions.prompt: Why is PNG a poor choice for photographs?

options.text: PNG can't be shown in browsers
PNG is lossless and produces very large files for photos; it's meant for graphics/transparency
PNG images always cause layout shift

questions.explanation: PNG is lossless, which bloats photographic content. Photos belong in AVIF/WebP/JPEG; reserve PNG for graphics needing sharp edges or transparency.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to prepare an optimized photo for the web.

items.text: Choose an efficient format (AVIF/WebP with fallback)
Add width/height and the right loading/priority attributes

questions.explanation: Pick the format, produce right-sized variants, compress, then write markup that reserves space and sets loading/priority appropriately.
